rows.citation: NeuroML organisation; contributors Sinha, A., Gleeson, P., Khandelwal, K., et al. (2025). neuroklea (formerly NeuroML/neuroml-ai): Knowledge vaLidated Expert AI assistant for neuroscience. GitHub repository.
rows.model_type: LLM agent and RAG assistant with a NeuroML MCP tool server (tooling for NeuroML/LEMS models, not a model-checking method)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - no mutation operators or recorded single-fault variants; the agent creates or edits code and models on user request.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - exposes a single run-LEMS-simulation tool (pynml/jLEMS); no stimulation battery or protocol set found in inspected files.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - no eFEL or feature-extraction code found in the repository file tree or NeuroML MCP tool module.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - nothing on choosing or minimising stimulation protocols.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - agent evaluator node only checks plan-step completion (marked WIP); no model-behaviour benchmark found.
rows.ai_transformations: yes - LangGraph coding agent with MCP tools (NeuroML template creation, LEMS runs, NeuroML-DB/OSB lookup, sandboxed Python) can generate or modify models.
rows.software: neuroklea https://github.com/NeuroML/neuroklea (GPL-3.0 per GitHub API; CHANGELOG says agent and MCP packages are unreleased WIP, tagged releases cover klea_utils/klea_rag only)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: A producer of AI-assisted NeuroML edits rather than a checker; NeuroSem would test whether such edits silently change behaviour using calibrated multi-protocol feature fingerprints.
rows.verification_method: GitHub REST API repos/NeuroML/neuroklea (description, created 2025-08-07, pushed 2026-09-11, GPL-3.0; repos/NeuroML/neuroml-ai resolves to NeuroML/neuroklea); git trees API file listing; README, CHANGELOG.md, mcp_pkg and agent_pkg READMEs via raw.githubusercontent.com; source of mcp_pkg/neuroml_mcp/tools/neuroml_tools.py and agent_pkg/klea_agent/nodes/evaluator.py.
rows.found_via: Repository linked from Sinha blog; GitHub REST API redirect from NeuroML/neuroml-ai (license GPL-3.0)

rows.citation: Cooper, J., Scharm, M., Mirams, G. R. (2016). The Cardiac Electrophysiology Web Lab. Biophysical Journal, 110(2), 292-300.
rows.model_type: cardiac cellular electrophysiology ODE models encoded in CellML
rows.controlled_mutations: no - no systematic mutants; one reported case where protocols exposed an erroneous versus corrected CellML model version.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - 23 virtual-experiment protocols (I-V curves, pacing rates, restitution, channel block, hypo/hyperkalaemia) run across 36 models.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - protocol post-processing yields AP properties, restitution and I-V curves; cardiac-specific outputs, not eFEL neuronal features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - protocols are hand-authored in a protocol language; no selection or minimisation of a protocol set.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - resource paper for characterising and comparing models; no discovery/held-out split or detection-rate evaluation.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-generated or automated model edits.
rows.software: Cardiac Electrophysiology Web Lab https://chaste.cs.ox.ac.uk/WebLab (URL as stated in the paper; built on Chaste; current availability not checked)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Already shows model/protocol separation and multi-protocol comparison can reveal model-version errors; NeuroSem adds NeuroML neuron models, mutation-calibrated tolerances, protocol-battery selection and held-out detection evaluation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.1016/j.bpj.2015.12.012 (title, authors, volume, issue, pages); Europe PMC REST search (PMID 26789753, PMC4724653, abstract); Europe PMC fullTextXML for PMC4724653 (methods and results sections scanned).
rows.found_via: Crossref title query 'Uncovering the Web Lab ...' (after WebSearch on functional curation); metadata verified via Crossref api.crossref.org/works

rows.citation: Jennings, M. W., Nithiarasu, P., Pant, S. (2024). Quantifying the efficacy of voltage protocols in characterising ion channel kinetics: A novel information-theoretic approach. International Journal for Numerical Methods in Biomedical Engineering, 40(5), e3815.
rows.model_type: ion-channel kinetics models under voltage clamp (parameter identifiability)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - parameters are sampled from priors for information analysis; no discrete fault or mutation operators.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - evaluates seven voltage-clamp protocols taken from the literature.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - uses POD-reduced current traces with mutual-information metrics, not interpretable electrophysiology features (abstract-level reading).
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - ranks protocols by a combined information criterion; framed as groundwork for future optimal design rather than optimisation itself.
rows.heldout_evaluation: unclear - metrics checked against known inverse-problem results; abstract describes no discovery/held-out model split.
rows.software: none identified (abstract only; full text not retrieved)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Scores voltage-clamp protocols for parameter identifiability of channel models; NeuroSem selects current-clamp batteries to detect behaviour-changing edits in neuron models, evaluated on held-out models and mutants.
rows.verification_method: Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.1002/cnm.3815 (metadata and abstract); Europe PMC REST search (PMID 38544355, abstract, keywords); Unpaywall (hybrid OA, CC-BY). Wiley pdfdirect full text blocked (HTTP 403 Cloudflare challenge), so methods were not read.
rows.found_via: WebSearch 'optimal experimental design voltage protocol ...'; metadata verified via Crossref api.crossref.org/works | Europe PMC '"optimal" AND "ion channel" AND "protocol" AND "experimental design"' | WebSearch OED voltage clamp query; PubMed query; Crossref

rows.multiple_stimuli: no - generic program test suites; no stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - not a neuroscience or signal-feature work.
rows.protocol_optimization: unclear - abstract does not mention test or mutant reduction; full text not read.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - survey paper; no held-out evaluation of its own.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Foundational mutation-testing prior art NeuroSem must cite; NeuroSem can only claim domain-specific NeuroML operators, simulation-based admissibility and calibrated feature tolerances, not mutation testing itself.

rows.citation: Harrold, M. J., Gupta, R., Soffa, M. L. (1993). A methodology for controlling the size of a test suite. ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology, 2(3), 270-285.
rows.controlled_mutations: no - reduction is driven by coverage of testing requirements (illustrated with data-flow testing), not mutants.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - not a neuroscience or signal-feature work.
rows.protocol_optimization: yes - selects a representative subset that keeps requirement coverage while removing redundant and obsolete tests.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - reports achievable reduction experimentally; no generalisation to unseen programs or fault families described in abstract.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Coverage-preserving suite reduction; NeuroSem's greedy battery would target mutant detection across stimulation protocols and test transfer to held-out models and a held-out mutation family.
